articles.title: Australian politics live: Lambie says Hanson hasn’t apologised to her over cartoon mocking her medical condition
articles.summary:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 20m agoLambie says Hanson hasn’t personally apologised over cartoon

blocks.caption: Benita Kolovos

blocks.text: Benita Kolovos
The husband of a Victorian Liberal party candidate has allegedly been assaulted during a confrontation over election signs.
A Liberal party spokesperson on Monday evening confirmed the husband of their candidate for Yan Yean, Amanda Dow, was involved in an alleged incident in Mernda yesterday afternoon.
They said:

double quotation markWe understand Ms Dow’s husband approached a member of the public who was removing Liberal party campaign signage and was allegedly assaulted. He suffered facial injuries and was taken to hospital and was discharged today.

Police confirmed a 59-year-old Mernda man had been charged with recklessly causing injury, criminal damage and unlawful assault over the incident, which they alleged occurred near Abundant Avenue and Bridge Inn Road at about 2pm yesterday.
“Police have been told the victim attended an address to retrieve political campaign signage when he was [allegedly] assaulted,” a spokesperson said.
They said the man has been bailed to appear before Heidelberg magistrates’ court on 1 February 2027.
The Liberal party spokesperson asked for privacy for Dow and her husband while he recovers.
It comes amid alarm about the safety of candidates in the wake of the Helen Haines attack and after Victoria’s emergency services minister said he thought he was being followed.
Lambie says Hanson hasn’t personally apologised over cartoon

blocks.caption: Josh Taylor

blocks.text: Josh Taylor

Independent senator Jacqui Lambie says the One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, has yet to personally apologise to her over her party’s “Please Explain” cartoon that poked fun at her medical condition, as the candidate behind the cartoon refuses to apologise.
Hanson publicly apologised for the cartoon that depicted Lambie saying “I can’t laugh because of my prolapsed vagina” and the video was subsequently removed from online platforms.
However, Lambie told ABC’s 7.30 last night that Hanson “hasn’t emailed, messaged, even sent me a nice little card and said, ‘I’m really sorry for doing that’”.

Mark Nicholson – who is running in the Victorian state election for One Nation and is cofounder of Stepmates Studio which makes the cartoons – told 7.30 it was his job to “pick on people in the public realm” and he would not apologise:
double quotation markNot right now. If I do anything that is apology-worthy, I’ll apologise.
Nicholson claimed he had “drawn quite a lot of attention” to the medical issue, rather than trivialising it.
Lambie said Nicholson should drop out of the election.
Welcome
Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it will be Kat Wong with the main action.

articles.title: Elvis Presley's music rights-holders sue Anthropic over songs used for AI training
articles.summary: Rights-holders of Elvis Presley's music catalog have sued Anthropic for more than $41 million US, accusing the artificial intelligence giant of tapping the King of Rock and Roll's songs without…

image.caption: AI company Anthropic is facing another lawsuit alleging it used copyrighted content without consent for training its AI models, this time brought by rights-holders of Elvis Presley's music catalog. (Dado Ruvic/Reuters)

blocks.text: Canada·New

Rights-holders of Elvis Presley's music catalog have sued Anthropic for more than $41 million US, accusing the artificial intelligence giant of tapping the King of Rock and Roll's songs without consent to train its AI models and 'infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale.'
King of Rock and Roll's hits remain influential and are still streamed today, say plaintiffs in copyright suit

Rights-holders of Elvis Presley's music catalog have sued Anthropic for more than $41 million US, accusing the artificial intelligence giant of tapping the King of Rock and Roll's songs without consent to train its AI models and "infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale."

A coalition of music and entertainment companies, trusts and individuals who together own the rights to 274 songs recorded and made famous by American music icon Presley filed the legal complaint on Friday in the Northern District of California, calling for a jury trial.

The lawsuit comes as the AI company filed papers Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever and amid wider warnings in recent months — including by Anthropic's CEO — about unfettered AI development as a potential risk to humanity.

Though nearly a half century has passed since his death in 1977, Presley's music continues to be influential and are still streamed today, the plaintiffs said in the filing, listing off a hit parade, from All Shook Up and Can't Help Falling in Love to A Little Less Conversation, Don't Be Cruel and (You're the) Devil In Disguise.

items: Nearly 50 years since his death, Elvis Presley continues to captivate new generations
Anthropic agrees to pay $1.5B US to settle author class action over AI training

blocks.text: The "iconic collective catalog contains some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history," the suit states.

The plaintiffs claim Anthropic has knowingly and willfully infringed copyright throughout the development of its Claude generative AI system, accusing the company of scraping song lyrics from approved internet sites — deliberately stripping out included Copyright Management Information such as songwriter, composer and music publisher credits — to create a database of copied content it then used to train AI models.

Pedestrians pass a tour bus with an image of Elvis Presley in 2024 shortly after Tennessee unveiled new legislation designed to protect songwriters, performers and other music industry professionals against the rise in artificial intelligence. (John Amis/The Associated Press)

Despite Anthropic having since introduced some changes aimed at preventing users of Claude from creating copyright-infringing musical content themselves, the lawsuit claims that the chatbot's outputs have continued to do exactly that.
After prompting Claude to recreate specific songs "for a modern audience," the plaintiffs wrote that the output included the following response:

"These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges. That's edging past 'inspired by' into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out," the filing notes.
LISTEN | Elvis Presley, 22, talks to CBC Radio after Ottawa show:
Archives5:48Elvis Presley in 1957: "You have to put on a show for people"

The Presley plaintiffs accuse Anthropic of direct copyright infringement, circumventing copyright protection measures and removing or altering copyright mangement information. They are seeking damages upwards of $41 million (all figures in US).
"We disagree with the claims and intend to ⁠defend this case fully," an Anthropic spokesperson told Reuters.
Lawsuits from creators, rights-holders

The lawsuit is the latest in a wave of legal action brought by writers, news outlets, visual artists, musicians and music publishers accusing AI tech companies of tapping copyrighted material to train their generative AI systems.
B.C. author leads lawsuits alleging big tech used writers' works to train AI
The companies have argued their systems make fair use of copyrighted material to create new content.

In 2023, a coalition of music publishers sued Anthropic, alleging the company infringed their copyright by using song lyrics from a vast range of hit artists — from the Rolling Stones and Bruno Mars, to the Beach Boys and Beyoncé — to train Claude.

The Presley complaint notes an expert witness for the music publishers in that 2023 case found multiple instances of Claude responding to users with lyrics from copyrighted songs verbatim (or virtually so) — including when the prompt was indirect (for example, asking for a song "in the style of" a particular artist).
That federal case is pending in Northern District of California after a transfer from Tennessee was granted in in mid-2024.

Also in 2023, a group of authors launched a class-action suit against Anthropic, accusing the company of using pirated copies of their books to train Claude without their permission. This past July, a U.S. judge approved a $1.5 billion settlement in the case.
With files from Reuters

articles.title: Microsoft gives voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees
articles.summary: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to more than a quarter of its global workforce — including in Canada — as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its…

image.caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stands in silhouette during the Microsoft Ignite conference in Chicago in 2024. The company offered buyouts to tens of thousands of employees on Monday. (Charles Rex Arbogast/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Business·New

Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to more than a quarter of its global workforce — including in Canada — as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its ‌massive AI investments.
Offer will be available to employees in Canada, India, the United ​Kingdom and the United States
· Thomson Reuters
· Posted: Oct 26, 2026 3:41 PM EDT | Last Updated: 19 minutes ago
Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to many staff members as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its ‌massive AI investments.

The offer was extended to about 60,000 employees, according to sources for CNBC, Reuters and Bloomberg. Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees ‌globally as of June 30, according to its annual filing, meaning more than a quarter of its global workforce would have received the buyout offer.

Staffers across the Windows maker would be eligible for the offers, including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, requesting anonymity ​as the matter was private. Units such as marketing, ​commercial business and security will be excluded, the source added.
In a memo, Microsoft's executive vice-president and chief people officer said the offer will be available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Microsoft didn't immediately respond to questions from CBC News about how many Canadians were offered the buyout.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company ​a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also ⁠gives participating organizations another ⁠way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," ‌chief people officer Amy Coleman said in a staff memo.
Block cuts nearly half its workforce, CEO cites AI tools

The company said it was a time-limited, voluntary program and built on insights gained from a previous voluntary retirement program. The eligible employees will receive details within the next few hours, it added.

Like other tech giants, Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data centres and chips, drawing scrutiny from investors over whether the returns will ⁠justify the staggering cost. The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close on Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion US in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year.

items: Meta to cut 8,000 jobs, Microsoft to offer voluntary buyouts for thousands
Microsoft to cut 4,800 jobs, overhaul Xbox unit

blocks.text: Shares of Microsoft, which had risen about 10 per cent this year, were up about 1 per cent on Monday. The development was first reported by Business Insider.
The company earlier this year offered ​voluntary buyouts to about 7 per cent of its U.S. workforce, or about 9,000 employees.

In July, Microsoft announced it would ⁠cut 4,800 jobs, or about 2.1 per cent of its global workforce, overhauling its Xbox gaming business and ⁠divesting up to five studios as it looks to boost returns after years ⁠of ⁠heavy investment in the division.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Florida parents say police called to 3-year-old's soccer game because kid was 'too good'
articles.summary: The parents of a 3-year-old soccer player in Florida say the police were called to a game this weekend because their son was dominating the ball. Police have confirmed with CBC News they were called…

image.caption: A 2023 file photo of a soccer camp in PEI. Police were called to a child's soccer game Saturday in Winter Park, Fla., over complaints of an 'unruly parent.' (Jane Robertson/CBC)

blocks.text: World·New

The parents of a 3-year-old soccer player in Florida say the police were called to a game this weekend because their son was dominating the ball. Police have confirmed with CBC News they were called to the game over reports of an "unruly parent."
The child, Nevada, is 'traumatized,' says his mother
In the viral video posted by his parents, a three-year-old central Florida boy dribbles the ball up the field, dodging the other pint-sized players and kicks it into the net as his parents cheer.
Then the boy, named Nevada, does it again. And again. And again.

Later in the same video, which has been viewed more than one million times on TikTok since it was posted Sunday, Nevada stands on the sidelines as his father says, "they called the police on a three-year-old because he was too good."
"Because he had the ball for too long, and nobody else could get the ball, so they called the police."

The reaction online was swift, with people equally enraged over the allegations and admiration for the preschooler's skills. In the TikTok comments, some called on the parents to sue, others alleged that calling the police was racist, and many commented on the "heartbreak" in the little boy's face when the police show up.
"I'm LIVID," children's entertainer and vocal children's rights advocate Ms. Rachel posted on Instagram Monday morning, calling on soccer stars and other athletes to support the child and his family.
"This is racist, sick, traumatizing and disgusting," she added.
Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III called the incident "crazy," writing on X that "punishing a 3 year old child for being too good at a sport is RIDICULOUS."

CBC News has reached out to Nevada's parents but has not yet heard back. The family already had a sizeable social media following on TikTok and Instagram, where they've documented Nevada's soccer skills over the years.

The Winter Park Police Department confirmed to CBC News Monday that officers were called to a children's soccer game Saturday after a league official "requested response to a disturbance between league officials and the parents of a player."
A screen shot of a post on Threads by children's entertainer Ms. Rachel on Monday. (@msrachelforlittles/Threads)
So, what actually happened?
The official called 911 at 9:53 a.m., according to the police incident report viewed by CBC News.
In a recording of the call provided by police, the official can be heard saying he has "an unruly parent here, calling me names and having me on Instagram."
He says the parent is being "really disruptive, like following me around and calling me names. I want her to be gone."
He describes her as a Black woman wearing pink.

items: Eastern Shore parent handed ban for harassing young minor hockey referee
Parent charged for threatening player during youth soccer game in Vaughan, police say

blocks.text: The incident report says the official told police the parents were upset about their son's playing time, while the parents said their child "was being scorned for playing too well and was being taken out of [the] game."

The Winter Park Police Department said the league had asked the family to leave and offered to refund its fees. When police arrived, the official asked officers to communicate that to the family, the department said.
A screen grab of an Instagram post by illustrator and activist Nikkolas Smith, in support of 3-year-old soccer player Nevada, posted on Monday. (@nikkolas_smith/Instagram)
"The family stated the game was over and they were leaving," the police statement says, adding that the family was co-operative and no one was arrested, trespassed or forced to leave the park.
The video posted by Nevada's parents shows a Black woman wearing pink speaking with two police officers. One tells her the league office should be reaching out soon about a refund.

In a separate video, the parents claim the soccer officials repeatedly pulled Nevada from the 30-minute game after he scored and that, as a result, he played only about 12 minutes — but still scored 10 goals.
Boy is 'traumatized,' says mother
The soccer league, i9 Sports Maitland/Winter Park, told CBC News in a statement Monday that it was aware of concerns about "an incident at a local i9 Sports program" and takes them very seriously.
"We have reached out to the family and have begun a review that includes speaking with those involved," the league said.

In an interview with The Breakfast Club, Nevada's mother, identified as Martasia Griffin, said Nevada has been targeted all season because of his talent and that, at this particular game, some parents complained that no one else could get the ball.

items: Canadian athletes detail experiences with racism in sports
UN human rights office slams racist abuse of Coco Gauff, calls for solidarity to help fight it

blocks.text: She said the league director agreed it was unfair to other children and offered Griffin a refund.
"I cannot explain to my three year old son that he cannot play today because he's so good. I continued to let him play until the police walked in," Griffin said.
Nevada, she told HuffPost in another interview Monday, is "traumatized."
An Instagram post by former U.S. soccer player Eddie Johnson in which he supports 3-year-old Nevada. (Eddie_Johnson7/Instagram)
"He still wants to play soccer. He just doesn’t want to go back to that place. I don’t think that’s how he should be thinking, that as a 3-year-old he did something wrong."

Former U.S. professional soccer player Eddie Johnson posted about Nevada several times on social media Sunday and Monday, saying the boy would be joining his soccer program and criticizing how he was treated at the game.
"They wanna dim his light," Johnson posted to his Instagram stories.
"They thought they were taking your dreams away, but in reality (made) you the most famous three-year-old in the world right now."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Natalie Stechyson has been a writer and editor at CBC News since 2021. She covers stories on social trends, families, gender, human interest, as well as general news. She's worked as a journalist since 2009, with stints at the Globe and Mail and Postmedia News, among others. Before joining CBC News, she was the parents editor at HuffPost Canada, where she won a silver Canadian Online Publishing Award for her work on pregnancy loss. You can reach her at natalie.stechyson@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
articles.summary: Maurene Comey believes she was let go from her job as a federal prosecutor because her father is the former FBI director.

blocks.text: The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled.

Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations.
Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay.
A spokesperson for the justice department said in a statement that it disagreed with the decision and "will appeal in due course".
In his ruling, Judge Furman said Comey's dismissal violated the US Constitution as well as his right to a fair legal process.
He said the US attorney general can fire federal prosecutors but only "in a particular manner and only for certain reasons".
Furman noted that in Comey's role, "she was assigned some of the country's highest profile cases and consistently received the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike".

Comey has worked on cases against the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, and hip-hop mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs, who was convicted on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends last year.
Furman ordered that Comey to be given back pay from July until December 2025, when she accepted a new job.
In a statement, Comey's lawyers said: "This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law".
Comey had previously said the only reason she was told about her firing was that it "came from Washington".

A complaint filed by her lawyers in September 2025 stated that they believed Comey had been fired "solely or substantially because her father is former FBI Director James B Comey, or because of her perceived political affiliation and beliefs, or both".
The justice department said in court filings that the decision was made by former Attorney General Pam Bondi.

The Trump administration has twice brought charges against James Comey, including for allegedly lying to Congress, but that case was dismissed by a judge who said the prosecutor who brought the case was unlawfully appointed.
Earlier this year, the justice department charged Comey with knowingly and wilfully making a threat to take the life of, and to inflict bodily harm, on the president. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The case stems from a 2025 Instagram post shared by Comey, which contained a photo of seashells on a beach arranged to read "86 47". "Eighty-six" is a slang term for "get rid of", and prosecutors allege it encourages violence against Trump.

articles.title: Netanyahu reportedly pressured military to attack Iran in run-up to election
articles.summary:
Israeli prime minister increases alarmist rhetoric as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in polls

Benjamin Netanyahu has resorted to increasingly alarmist rhetoric and reportedly put…
articles.byline: Emma Graham-Harrison and Julian Borger in Jerusalem

blocks.text: Benjamin Netanyahu has resorted to increasingly alarmist rhetoric and reportedly put pressure on Israel’s military to take action against Iran as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in the polls ahead of Tuesday’s close-run elections.
The Israeli prime minister posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear mushroom cloud destroying Tel Aviv, telling Israeli voters to choose him or risk nuclear annihilation.

“Anyone who cares about their own physical existence, that of their family, and their loved ones should have a trembling hand before voting for [the opposition],” he wrote in a social media post about Iran’s nuclear programme.

blocks.caption: An AI-generated image of a nuclear strike on Tel Aviv was posted on Netanyahu’s X account on Sunday.  Photograph: X/Benjamin Netanyahu

blocks.text: Israel’s Channel 12 news reported that the prime minister and the armed forces chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, clashed in recent days over a directive to the military which could “potentially spark an immediate conflagration with Iran at a very sensitive juncture”, by provoking a miscalculation by Iran.
Zamir is reported to have requested the directive, the details of which were not specified, to be presented to him in writing.
Netanyahu denied the report, and the defence ministry later denied any intention to carry out military operations against Iran.
On Monday however, CNN reported that Netanyahu had tried to convince Donald Trump to launch a renewed assault on Iran in recent weeks, renewing the war both men started in February.
The report, confirming an earlier account in the Financial Times, said Trump had ruled out any such action until US congressional elections next week.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) issued a statement on Monday that stopped well short of a denial of the press reports. It simply insisted that its decisions were based exclusively on “security, professional, objective and national considerations”.
Netanyahu’s warnings were a marked contrast with his triumphalism in the immediate wake of the wars on Iran that launched last year and this spring.

In March Netanyahu said Israeli and US strikes had destroyed Iran’s ability to enrich uranium and produce ballistic missiles, and in 2025 he claimed a “historic victory” over Iran that would stand for generations.

Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the opposition bloc and Netanyahu’s most likely challenger for the prime minister’s job, expressed his confidence in Zamir. “We won’t allow the IDF to be turned into a pawn in Netanyahu’s survival campaign,” said Eisenkot, who is a retired general.

blocks.caption: Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the opposition bloc, is the most likely challenger to Netanyahu as prime minister.  Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA

blocks.text: Most polls suggest the mainly centre-right opposition bloc led by Eisenkot is poised to win more seats in Israel’s Knesset than the Netanyahu coalition, but neither would be able to muster the 61 seats necessary for a majority government.

The opposition would most likely be able to gather a majority and topple Netanyahu in coalition with parties representing Palestinians with Israeli citizenship, roughly a fifth of the population. But conservatives inside the Eisenkot bloc have ruled out such a coalition, raising the prospect of a minority government, another round of elections and a possible Netanyahu resurgence.

As the elections drew closer, Netanyahu framed the country’s choice as existential. He told Channel 14, which has acted as his lead cheerleader in the Israeli media: “There is a single fundamental issue here – our existence.”

He described the opposition bloc as the “left” in alliance with Palestinians, and enemies of the country. “We see what is happening in Europe. The alliance between the left and Islam might destroy the state of Israel,” he said.

The main opposition parties are rightwing or centre-right, sharing Netanyahu’s adamant opposition to the establishment of a Palestinian state, and who have largely supported the war in Gaza. Some opposition leaders have ruled out any kind of political alliance with Palestinian Israeli parties, who could emerge from the elections holding the balance of power in the Knesset. Palestinians in the occupied territories do not have the vote.

The opposition bloc is held together more by its shared antipathy to Netanyahu, who has dominated the Israeli political scene over the past three decades and veered increasingly towards authoritarianism, seeking to limit the independence of the judiciary and turn the police and Shin Bet internal security service into political tools.
The prime minister is also in the midst of a trial on corruption charges, and his legal jeopardy could increase if he loses his grip on power.

blocks.caption: Benjamin Netanyahu has been emphasising in his campaign the support he has from Donald Trump. Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

blocks.text: In the closing stages of the campaign, Netanyahu has also emphasised the overt support he enjoys from Donald Trump, who repeated his endorsement on Sunday in a social media post, saying “When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding warrior prime minister!”

The Israeli outlet Walla News reported that this repeat endorsement was a result of relentless pressure from Netanyahu’s office. It is unclear, however, whether Trump’s support will carry any weight with the electorate. The US president’s earlier “total endorsement” on 18 October made no visible difference to the polls.

In one survey, 64% of Israelis questioned said it would not influence their vote, and 17% said it made them less likely to back Netanyahu, against 12% who said it had deepened their resolve to support Netanyahu’s Likud party.

In the closing stages of the closely fought campaign, Netanyahu has also forecast growing financial isolation, saying billions of dollars in annual military aid from the US would dry up soon, and drew a rare public rebuke from the central bank for a repeated claim that Israel could use cryptocurrencies to dodge escalating global sanctions.

“Cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means to circumvent sanctions,” the Bank of Israel said on Sunday evening. “The right course for the Israeli economy is to maintain economic relations with our primary trading partners and to focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy.”

Netanyahu had already laid out a forecast for a bleak, isolated future a year ago, when he said Israel might need to become a militarised “super Sparta”, then rowed back again in the face of fierce criticism from a horrified Israeli public.

His return to this rhetoric and the tactics of fear, particularly after unexpected losses for far-right allies in Serbia and Brazil, raised questions about whether the ultimate political survivor may finally be on the ropes.

Few among his allies or enemies expected his government to survive long after 7 October, much less complete its term. But the majority of polls have been clear for more than two years that his current coalition looks set to lose its slim majority.

articles.title: 'Crypto King' trial hears recording of Aiden Pleterski admitting $300M fund 'never existed'
articles.summary: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski admitted his $300-million fund never existed in a June 2022 audio recording played in court at his fraud trial in Toronto on Monday.

image.caption: Self-described “Crypto King” Aiden Pleterski is shown in various photos. (aiden.ptrs/Instagram)

blocks.text: Toronto·New
Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski admitted his $300-million fund never existed in a June 2022 audio recording played in court at his fraud trial in Toronto on Monday.
Retired Durham police officer who invested with Pleterski testifies at fraud trial

Pleterski, 27, was providing screenshots and videos of his FXChoice trading platform account with a balance more than $311 million to concerned investors just weeks before the recorded meeting with three investors, Pleterski and a lawyer he brought with him, Ontario Superior Court heard.
One of those three investors, Chris Winn, started testifying remotely Monday morning.

The retired Durham Regional Police officer is the last of 14 witnesses the Crown has called in their prosecution. Winn, who invested a combined $450,000 himself and through a holding company, said he got back $330,000. He testified to attending two meetings at the home of another investor with Pleterski.

Chris Winn, a retired Durham Regional Police officer, invested a combined $450,000 himself and through a holding company with Aiden Pleterski, and testified in Ontario Superior Court that he got back $330,000. (Monica Winn/Facebook)
"He told us basically he hadn't traded any of the money and basically it's a Ponzi scheme," said Winn.

items: ‘Crypto King’ spent $16.3M of investor funds on cars, credit cards, jets, security, accountant testifies
Real estate developer testifies he gave 'Crypto King’ Aiden Pleterski $4.5M to invest

blocks.text: Pleterski, who is representing himself at trial, has pleaded not guilty to fraud over $5,000 and money laundering.
Near the beginning of the roughly three-hour recording from the second meeting, this exchange between Pleterski and the two other investors present, Brad Rogers and Jason Affleck, occurs:
Pleterski: "The $300 million it was –"
Rogers: "Never existed, you said."
Pleterski: "It never existed."
Affleck: "But how was that shown to us on a screen, and a piece of paper, was that Photoshopped? Or was that documented? Like how was that — we saw it?"
Pleterski: "Mitch showed you the picture and all that based on whatever, then that account basically never existed."

Earlier in the trial, another investor and former friend of Pleterski's, Mitchell Learning, testified he went looking for "proof in person" of how much money was in Pleterski's investment account — after receiving a screenshot and video showing the FX Choice with a $311-million balance.

Learning went to Pleterski's lakefront mansion in Burlington, Ont., in June 2022 and was able to access Pleterski's email account on his computer. He testified that he found an email from FXChoice confirming Pleterski had deleted that account.

items: 'Crypto King' investor recounts the moment he learned $311M investment fund didn’t exist

blocks.text: Learning told the court Pleterski admitted to losing the money trading the year before and said to Learning that he'd been paying investors back with other investors' funds since then.
Mitchell Learning outside Ontario Superior Court in Toronto on Oct. 9 at the trial of Pleterski. (Mehrdad Nazarahar/CBC)
The investor meeting with Winn, Pleterski and others took place about a week after Learning testified Pleterski confessed what was going on to Learning in June 2022, according to the recording.
"Since January, I've refunded $700,000, lost it, I've refunded $1 million, lost it, I've refunded $300,000, lost it," said Pleterski at the recorded meeting.
"That was money that was taken in from investors."
A couple of investors talking over each other say "from us" and "we paid all your debts."
‘I'm sitting here trying to make it right': Pleterski

Over the course of the meeting, the investors try to suggest that Pleterski liquidate his assets and put them into a business controlled by the investors. From there, they would supervise Pleterski conducting trades to make everyone's money back. They also regularly repeat they don't trust Pleterski because he's lied to them and make multiple references to him going to jail.
"This is one of the biggest Ponzi schemes in f–king Ontario," said Winn, in one of those instances. "It'll be front page of the paper."
Pleterski enters Ontario Superior Court in Toronto on Oct. 5. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)
After another part of the recording where investors talk about Pleterski lying, he raises his voice in response.
"If I had a malicious intent with any of this, I wouldn't be sitting in front of you guys, I'd be on a f--king plane getting out of here right now," said Pleterski.
"I could have been gone long, a long f--king time ago, but I'm sitting here trying to make it right. Everybody's f--king leaning on me."
Pleterski also argues he knows how to trade, but said in the recording that he's not in the headspace to do it well given the stress he's under.

Since the start of his trial in early October, the Crown has alleged that Pleterski guaranteed the money his investors gave him for trading, but never actually invested the funds, instead spending the money on himself. Just over a week ago, the court was presented with the first detailed evidence in support of that aspect of the prosecution's case.
$16.3M spent on himself: accountant

A senior forensic accountant who reviewed Pleterski's financial records testified that investors provided Pleterski with more than $36.3 million and none of those funds were ever sent to FXChoice, the trading platform investor contracts said Pleterski would use on their behalf.

Instead, Albert Ciorma from the Ontario Securities Commission said his forensic audit found Pleterski spent about $5.6 million on luxury vehicles, $4.9 million on credit card bills, $870,000 on travel and private jets and $598,000 on security. Pleterski also gave nearly $3.7 million to his parents and took $609,000 in cash advances from a credit card, Ciorma said.
Albert Ciorma, a senior forensic accountant with the Ontario Securities Commission, testified earlier this month in Pleterski's fraud trial. (Pam Davies/CBC)
Altogether, those expenses total more than $16.3 million. Pleterski also paid out another $16.1 million to investors from the funds he received, according to Ciorma.
Winn's testimony and the rest of the audio recording of the investor meeting he attended are expected to be heard in court Monday afternoon.
After that's completed, Pleterski will have the opportunity to call witnesses and testify himself if he chooses.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Nicole Brockbank is a reporter for CBC Toronto's Enterprise Unit. She digs up, researches and reports GTA-focused investigative and enterprise stories. nicole.brockbank@cbc.ca

articles.title: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
articles.summary: The term "maxxing" is used as an adjective, adverb, noun and verb by many in Gen Z and Gen Alpha to describe an emphasis in optimisation.

blocks.text: Americans have gone all in on "maxxing", making it the 2026 Word of the Year for Dictionary.com.

Short for maximising, the term "can be used on its own or added to the end of any word to convey you're doing something to the fullest or optimizing it as much as possible", Dictionary.com said in a statement.
It's a major departure from two years ago, when the site, after analysing US social media trends, news stories, and search data, chose "demure" as word of the year. Last year's was "67".
"Maxxing is the linguistic manifestation of a culture increasingly preoccupied with getting the most out of everything," said Steve Johnson, director of lexicography for the Dictionary Media Group.

Digital media used "maxxing" nearly 19 times more in August 2026 compared to the 2025 monthly average, Dictionary.com found. The site also considered affordability, data centre, odyssey, and the shortened form of uncle, "unc", as potential words of the year.
On social media, many people in Generation Z and younger - those under 30 - post extensively about their maxxing efforts to achieve all sorts of perfection.
Influencers focused on fitness and wellness post about "proteinmaxxing" and "fibermaxxing". Those giving their full attention to improving sleep habits say they are "sleepmaxxing".

The influencer Clavicular has gained thousands of followers as he chronicles his extreme "looksmaxxing" - working to meet a set of prescribed criteria for attractiveness, with particular importance given to jawlines, eyes and physique.

"Whatever we're doing, we want to push it further," Johnson said. "But its expanding uses also reveal how people are responding to that impulse. Some embrace it. Some exaggerate it for laughs. Others subvert it entirely to describe stepping back from the relentless pursuit of more."
People were playing with the term - and idea - for decades before Clavicular started posting videos.
In the opening song for the 1990's television show The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, for example, Will Smith raps: "Chillin' out, maxin', relaxin' all cool.".

articles.title: iPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handset
articles.summary:
Company says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social media

Owners of the new foldable iPhone are reporting cracks in the device’s screen,…

blocks.text: Owners of the new foldable iPhone are reporting cracks in the device’s screen, as Apple confirmed an issue with a “small number” of units.

Reports of cracks have emerged on Reddit and social media platforms since the handset went on general sale globally on Friday. Experts said there had been too few examples to determine whether there was a more serious problem with Apple’s first foldable device, which retails from $1,999 (£1,499).
Apple confirmed some devices had been affected by a display glitch.

“We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement,” it said.
One user in Australia reported that their Duo had cracked within six hours of taking ownership of it and posted their experience on Reddit.

“I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen,” they wrote alongside an image of the phone showing an apparent display malfunction where a white strip of light ran along one half of the screen.
“As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge.”

They said their local Apple store had replaced the phone immediately. The Guardian has been unable to verify the user’s claims. Another user in Australia posted that they had heard “almost a cracking noise” on their handset, which resulted in a similar screen malfunction.

blocks.caption: IPhone Duo handsets on display at an Apple store in London. Photograph: Kin Cheung/AP

blocks.text: A report by the Bloomberg news service also highlighted similar issues among users in the US and India.
Apple believes the affected units are showing defects quickly after use. It said the response from early users had been “incredibly positive”.

The company said demand had been “nothing short of extraordinary” for the iPhone Duo, its most high-profile product launch under the company’s new chief executive, John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September.
after newsletter promotion

The device has sold out and the next round of shipments is not expected until January, according to a report in the Economic Daily, a publication based in Taiwan, the home country of Foxconn, Apple’s main device manufacturer.

Francisco Jeronimo, the vice-president of data and analytics at IDC, a tech research company, said it was too early to tell whether the screen issue was significant. “This is quite common when a new product comes to market,” he said.

Citing similar problems at Samsung in 2019, he said: “What matters now is how the company responds … Samsung experienced problems with the original Galaxy Fold in 2019, but it also showed that a fast and transparent response can contain the damage to a category.
“Apple said that any customer with problems should ask for a replacement, which is the right first step.”

Ben Wood, the chief analyst at the research firm CCS, said he was taking a very cautious view of the Duo screen problem and that there was as yet no evidence of a more widespread issue with the device.

articles.title: Nigeria Ebola patient flown to Switzerland, Congo health worker killed as 4 countries deal with outbreak
articles.summary: Officials on opposite sides of the African continent are trying to determine how a woman diagnosed with Ebola in Nigeria's capital last week contracted the deadly virus without having visited the…

image.caption: A patient suspected to have Ebola is transferred in a isolation unit from a rescue aircraft to a Swiss Air Rescue helicopter at Zurich Airport on Monday, after a medical evacuation flight from Nigeria's capital Abuja. (Michael Buholzer/Keystone/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Officials on opposite sides of the African continent are trying to determine how a woman diagnosed with Ebola in Nigeria's capital last week contracted the deadly virus without having visited the Democratic Republic of Congo — the epicentre of one of the worst human outbreaks of the virus in history.

The woman, an Ugandan-born Swiss citizen, was transported on a medical evacuation flight from Abuja to Switzerland on Monday, as questions linger about how she may have contracted the virus while visiting Uganda.
Meanwhile, a health-care worker in the D.R.C. is dead after being attacked over the weekend, as the outbreak continues to spread and claim more lives.

D.R.C.'s Health Ministry's most recent data indicates more than 9,800 cases, including more than 4,700 deaths, have been recorded since the start of the outbreak in May, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history.
Here's a look at the latest developments in the four countries that have been affected by the Ebola outbreak.
Children bear brunt of DRC’s Ebola outbreak
Nurse killed in Democratic Republic of Congo
A nurse was killed and a health worker severely injured after being attacked while responding to an Ebola alert in D.R.C., according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
It was the latest in a series of attacks on health workers and responders that authorities say is hampering efforts to slow the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in the world.

The attack took place Saturday in the town of Bafwasende in the country's eastern Tshopo province, one of eight provinces affected by the outbreak, WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a post on X on Sunday.
Doctors Without Borders physicians treat a patient inside the Kitatumba Ebola treatment centre in Butembo, D.R.C., on Sept. 23. (Gradel Muyisa Mumbere/Reuters)

items: Fears of a pan-African Ebola crisis growing as fourth country reports first case
Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak is now the deadliest in its history

blocks.text: "Everyone working to protect communities from this deadly disease must be able to work in dignity and safety. Healthcare must always be protected," he said.
WHO regional director for Africa, Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, also condemned the attack on X.
"Misinformation and fear must never fuel violence," he said. Local authorities have not yet commented on the attack or the suspects.
Last month, a Congolese politician was beaten to death in North Kivu — a war-torn province that that has the second-highest number of confirmed cases but the highest fatality ratio.

It happened after he publicly defended the government's response to Ebola. He had been calling on the public to obey response measures, particularly social distancing and handwashing, on a radio show.
Back in May at the start of the outbreak, two tents at health centres were set alight in two separate attacks in just one week by angry residents.
There is widespread distrust of the country's government because of how it has managed past Ebola outbreaks as well as chronic corruption.
In a positive development, Ghebreyesus shared news from a treatment clinic in Ituri province, which has recorded the highest number of confirmed cases since the outbreak began.

In a post on X, he shared a video from the community of Mongbwalu showing health workers dancing as they discharged their two remaining patients and noted that no new positive cases had been confirmed at the clinic in the past five days.
Ebola patient flown from Nigeria to Switzerland

The Swiss woman being treated for Ebola in Nigeria was medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband Monday, officials said, as Nigerian authorities continued monitoring 52 people who had been in contact with her.
Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad Pate said the woman, the country's first case in the current outbreak, left the capital, Abuja, early Monday with his approval.
Her condition had improved significantly, and she was stable, conscious and able to communicate, he said.
"This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place," Pate wrote on X. Her husband, a Swiss diplomat in Nigeria, has shown no symptoms.
He later confirmed the couple arrived safely in Switzerland and the woman is receiving care in Geneva, while her husband is in isolation at a hospital in Zurich.

The WHO's Janabi, said the evacuation was arranged because the couple are Swiss citizens and that Nigerian medical teams had stabilized the woman after treating her through the acute phase of the illness.
LISTEN | First human clinical trial of new Ebola vaccine underway in Halifax:
The Current19:31As Ebola spreads, Canadian scientists work on a vaccine
Switzerland will take over her care and monitor her husband, while Nigeria will continue following 52 other contacts, Janabi said.

"With the evacuation of the patient and her husband, Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases," he said, stressing that vigilance remained critical. Pate said containment measures remained in place and urged Nigerians to remain vigilant.
The woman tested positive after returning to Abuja from Uganda.

Nigerian authorities said Friday they had yet to establish how she contracted the virus. Switzerland's Foreign Ministry told The Associated Press that she had not visited D.R.C. and was believed to have been infected while travelling to Uganda with her husband.
The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said the first patients in Nigeria and Kenya had both travelled through Uganda's Entebbe International Airport on Oct. 3.

Travellers stand next to a banner displayed by a health screening station at Nigeria's Murtala Muhammed International Airport, in Lagos, following reports of an Ebola case in the country last week. (Sodiq Adelakun/Reuters)
Uganda implements quarantine rules
Uganda says it is investigating ​the Nigerian case, but insists the country remains Ebola-free after declaring an end to its latest outbreak in July.

But the government is reinforcing border controls to stop the spread of the deadly Ebola virus and now requires citizens returning from neighboring D.R.C. to spend 21 days in quarantine at their own expense, the Health Ministry said Sunday.
It first established border controls in May, restricting all but essential travellers, including humanitarian workers and truck drivers, subject to screening.
Travellers with a history of travel to Congo cannot transit through Uganda, including on chartered flights.

Under the new measures announced Sunday, nonessential Congolese travellers will be returned through the nearest border crossing at their own expense, while those entering illegally face prosecution, the Ugandan ministry said.

Screening has intensified at Entebbe International Airport and land borders and all arrivals must complete a passenger locator form and undergo health screening, including diplomats and United Nations personnel.

A Kenyan health worker checks the temperatures of travellers crossing from Uganda to Kenya as part of measures to contain the spread of Ebola virus, in Busia, Kenya, on Oct. 15. (Andrew Kasuku/The Associated Press)
Kenya clears Ebola patient contacts
Kenya on Monday released from quarantine the first group of people who came into contact with its index Ebola patient, a milestone in its efforts ‌to contain cases to a single infection cluster.
The 20 people released completed 21 days of monitoring without developing Ebola symptoms and are in good health, ​the director general in Kenya's Health Ministry, Patrick ​Amoth, said in a statement.

Kenya has reported nine Ebola cases so far, two of whom have died. ​The remaining seven patients are stable and receiving treatment, ⁠Amoth said, adding ⁠that 98 others still ‌in quarantine would be released in four waves beginning on Nov. 3.
"This is a milestone worth celebrating," Amoth said. "It is also a reminder that the work ⁠is not yet done."
Kenya's first case died in a hospital in Nairobi on Oct. 5, after which eight others fell ill ‌while in quarantine. It announced on Friday that a second person had died.
Amoth said ⁠those leaving quarantine posed no risk to their families or communities where they live and urged Kenyans to welcome them home. "We cannot afford to drop our vigilance," he said.
Ebola outbreak now deadliest in Congo’s history

articles.title: Police locate vehicle allegedly used by Toronto mother to abduct 3 children
articles.summary: Toronto police say they have found a vehicle believed to have been used to abduct three children from Scarborough on Friday, but the children and their mother have not been found.

image.caption: From left, Daniel, six, Irina, three, and four-month-old Anastasia. The three children were having a semi-supervised visit with a relative on Friday, when their mother took them and fled, according to police. (Toronto Police Service)

blocks.text: Toronto·Breaking
Toronto police say they have found a vehicle believed to have been used to abduct three children from Scarborough on Friday, but the children and their mother have not been found.
Children, mother not yet found, police say
In a news release Monday, police said the mother of the three children, Somerda Miclescu, 22, was believed to be driving a 2017 White Ford Expedition vehicle with Ontario license plate DJJS 875.
Police did not say where or when they found the vehicle.

Daniel, six, Irina, three, and Anastasia, four months, were having a semi-supervised visit with a relative on Friday, when polices say their mother took them and fled. Police say the children's mother does not have legal custody of them.
"Efforts to locate them remain ongoing," police said in the release.
Police described the mother as 5 feet 7 inches, about 180 pounds, with long, black hair. Police said she was last seen wearing a long black skirt and a dark-coloured top.
Somerda Miclescu is wanted by police for allegedly abducting her three children. (Toronto Police Service)
Police first responded to a call at about 11:30 a.m. Friday for an abduction in the Midland Avenue and Eglinton Avenue East area.

items: Toronto police seeking mother, 22, for allegedly abducting her 3 children

blocks.text: Police have named Ionut Stroe, 25, who owns vehicle in which Miclescu fled, as a person of interest.
Stroe is also wanted for four counts of failing to comply with a release order, unrelated to the abduction.
Police described him as being around 5 feet 11 inches, 235 pounds, with a tattoo on his right forearm.

articles.title: Quebec's Spa Nordik introduces new safety measures following sexual assault allegations
articles.summary: Nordik Spa Village in Chelsea, Que., has announced new measures to protect clients amid a class action lawsuit alleging sexual assault that implicates 36 massage therapists who worked there over a…

image.caption: In a list outlined on its website, Spa Nordik says massage therapists will now undergo criminal background checks and get training on consent and the prevention of sexual violence. (Jean-Sébastien Marier/CBC)

blocks.text: Ottawa

Nordik Spa Village in Chelsea, Que., has announced new measures to protect clients amid a class action lawsuit alleging sexual assault that implicates 36 massage therapists who worked there over a 19-year period.
Background checks, consent forms, and security personnel among new steps
Nordik Spa Village in Chelsea, Que., has announced new measures to protect clients amid a class action lawsuit alleging sexual assault that implicates 36 massage therapists over a 19-year-period.
In a list outlined on its website, the spa says massage therapists will now undergo criminal background checks and get training on consent and the prevention of sexual violence.
They'll also be "required to maintain good standing with a recognized professional association."
Massage services will be relegated to their own floor with security personnel, the spa says.

items: Class action alleging sexual assaults at Spa Nordik to proceed

blocks.text: Other measures include an electronic consent form that clients will be able to update throughout their massage and a requirement for therapists to obtain consent before massaging "sensitive areas."
The spa defines those as the "buttocks [and] upper inner thighs" and the "pectoral area."
Clients will also have the option to have the audio of their session recorded. A new complaint process for clients is also being implemented, the spa says.
Founder 'deeply shaken'

In a statement shared on social media, Groupe Nordik founder Martin Paquette wrote that the company is committed to the safety of its clients, adding that he was "deeply shaken," and "angry" when he learned of the allegations.
"No one should ever have to go through something like that in a place dedicated to well-being," he wrote.
Paquette also called for stronger government oversight of Quebec's massage therapy sector.
"Unfortunately, what has happened at our establishment is not unique to Nordik," he said.

articles.title: Chris Brown gets suspended 8-month sentence for 2023 nightclub attack, avoiding jail
articles.summary: Singer Chris Brown has avoided immediate imprisonment for attacking a music producer in a London nightclub in 2023, with a U.K. judge handing him an eight-month suspended sentence.

image.caption: R&B singer Chris Brown leaves a London court on Monday after he was given an eight-month suspended sentence for attacking a music producer in a crowded nightclub in 2023. (Chris J Ratcliffe/Reuters)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Singer Chris Brown has avoided immediate imprisonment for attacking a music producer in a London nightclub in 2023, with a U.K. judge handing him an eight-month suspended sentence.
R&B singer pleaded guilty to attacking music producer with a tequila bottle

"Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also others nearby," Judge Tony Baumgartner said at London's Southwark Crown Court on Monday.

Brown, 37, had pleaded guilty to charges stemming from the attack at the city's Tape nightclub in February 2023. Brown struck Abraham Diaw twice in the head with a tequila bottle and continued to attack him until restrained, Baumgartner recounted Monday.
"The repeated use of a glass bottle against the head made your conduct particularly dangerous," he told Brown.

Brown's vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, who also participated in the attack had, like Brown, pleaded guilty to charges of affray in July, after denying the more serious charges of assault and and attempting to inflict grievous bodily harm.

Affray is a criminal charge for using or threatening physical violence in a way that causes a person to fear for their safety. Brown was facing a maximum three years in prison for what prosecutors described as the "unprovoked attack."

But Brown was spared a jail stint — his eight-month sentence has been suspended for 12 months, meaning he’ll only go to prison to serve those eight months if he commits another offence within the next year.
Omololu Omari Akinlolu, Brown's voice coach and co-defendant, walks outside the Southwark Crown Court in London, on Oct. 28, 2025. (Isabel Infantes/Reuters)
Akinlolu, 40, who received a four-month sentence, also had his suspended for 12 months.
Brown has been embroiled in legal trouble over violence numerous times, and has an extensive criminal record.

In 2009, he was sentenced to five years probation after pleading guilty to assaulting his then-girlfriend, singer Rihanna. Brown choked and punched Rihanna, leaving visible injuries on her face, and threatened her life, according to a police affidavit. Following another misdemeanor assault charge for attacking a man outside a hotel in Washington, D.C., Brown went to jail in 2014.

items: Chris Brown pleads guilty to charge over London nightclub fight
Brown free on bail while awaiting trial over London nightclub incident

blocks.text: The highly publicized 2009 case, as well as continued allegations of violent behaviour over the years, has led to protests and calls for Brown to be blacklisted by the industry. Yet, the R&B singer has continued to have a successful career, scoring Grammy awards for best R&B album in 2011 and 2025.

Brown was arrested in May 2025 in connection with the nightclub incident after he returned to Britain for the first time since the attack. He was initially denied bail, but was released after promising to pay a £5 million ($9.3 million Cdn) security fee.

items: BTS members cause outcry after attending Chris Brown show in Toronto

blocks.text: Baumgartner said that Brown’s "initiation of the violence, the repeated bottle strikes," and his continued aggression as Diaw tried to move away all were serious considerations in deciding the sentence.
He cited the absence of planning, the short duration of the assault — about 20 seconds — and Brown’s young children in his decision to limit the sentence to eight months.
Brown and Akinlolu each were required to pay a portion of the prosecution’s costs.

In England and Wales, custodial sentences of 12 months or less are automatically suspended unless the judge assesses that there are exceptional circumstances that require the offender to be immediately imprisoned.
Brown’s lawyer, Sallie Bennett-Jenkins called him "a dedicated, loving and loyal father to four ​children" and said he was sorry for this “ugly and unattractive incident.”
Brown, seen here outside a London court in July 2025, has been embroiled in legal trouble over violence numerous times, and has an extensive criminal record. (Chris J. Ratcliffe/Reuters)

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: Major clean-up under way after two storms cause havoc in Britain
articles.summary: More strong winds forecast after Boelo and Austen bring travel disruption and flooding and kill two people
articles.byline: Mark Brown North of England correspondent

blocks.text: A major clean-up operation was under way on Monday after weekend storms caused heartache and havoc with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come.
Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, struck parts of the UK, bringing widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations.
The Energy Networks Association, which represents operators in the UK and Ireland, said 90,000 customers were still without power on Monday morning. That figure was later down to 39,000.

The association’s chief executive, Lawrence Slade, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that disruption had been widespread with operators having to restore power to about 700,000 customers over the weekend.
He said Friday, Saturday and Sunday had been particularly challenging. “It certainly was a tough one. One of the problems was how quickly Boelo followed after Austen.”

Another issue was that there was no letup in the strong winds, widely 50-70mph and up to 85mph in northern Scotland. “Until that weather system passes we can’t safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up etc.”

blocks.caption: Storm Boelo causes severe flooding in town centre of Largs, Scotland

blocks.text: The weather was much milder on Monday but the Met Office said more strong winds were on the way and issued two yellow weather warnings. One is in place from 6pm until 3am on Tuesday, covering western coastal areas from Cornwall up to south-west Scotland. Gusts of up to 65mph could hit exposed coastal areas, accompanied by heavy rain at times. The Met Office warned people to take care near cliffs and be aware of strong waves.

The second warning is in place from 3am to 9pm on Tuesday and covers most of Scotland. Forecasters said winds of 50-60mph were likely to be quite widespread with gusts up to 70mph in the far north. It warned of possible travel cancellations, road closures and more power cuts.
The weekend storms led to two deaths, authorities said. A 60-year-old man was hit by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway while a man in his 20s died in Finchley, north London.
The 60-year-old was named on Monday afternoon as Richard Baines, the curator of Logan Botanic Garden near Port Logan.

David Knott, the director of horticulture at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, said Baines would be remembered for his “passion and enthusiasm for plants … significantly increasing and expanding the plant collection at Logan”.

There was flooding in several parts of Scotland with dramatic footage from Largs showing flood water cascading through the town centre. One resident said it was the highest she had ever seen in 36 years of living there.

Staff at the Thai restaurant Tha-Tien-Thai shared a video of their kitchen overrun by water with the desperate caption: “There is nothing left.” They said its doors would be closed for the foreseeable future “due to larger flood restoration than originally planned”.
Robyn Cryans, an executive assistant from Renfrew is on holiday in Cyprus and woke to see pictures, taken by a neighbour, of her Nissan Micra Sport submerged back at home.

“It is very upsetting, a bit stressful” she said. “It was unexpected considering we’ve got a £10m flood barrier literally just down the road which is supposed to activate if the Clyde bursts its banks.”

blocks.caption: A downed tree in Gladstone Park, London, on Sunday after strong winds overnight.  Photograph: Martin Evans/PA

blocks.text: She is scheduled to fly back tomorrow and fully expects to find her flat damaged. “I’m obviously very upset about it, but at the end of the day it’s material objects. It could have been a lot worse.”
In Aberdeenshire, 13 primary schools without power were shut on Monday, and Ellon academy was closed because of storm damage. Ten primary schools were shut in the Highlands.
Scotland’s first minister, John Swinney, met senior politicians, emergency teams and forecasters on Sunday to discuss the ongoing response to the weather, amid the warnings of more to come.

Emergency services were called to a flooded care home in Saltcoats, North Ayrshire, on Sunday evening. Police Scotland said everyone at the care home was accounted for, road closures were in place and officers were expected to remain on site overnight to assist.

There was also travel disruption, with being flights diverted from landing at Leeds Bradford, England’s highest airport, and others cancelled. Most train services were getting back to normal although operators advised customers to check before they travelled.

The storms brought a number of event cancellations including the Sunday racing at Aintree, abandoned because of the high winds. The Guardian’s live blog of the terrible tea-time Sunderland v Leeds goalless draw summed up the action: “And the winner is … the wind.”

articles.title: AI company Anthropic files its IPO in hopes of raising $100 billion
articles.summary: Anthropic has filed paperwork for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest in history. The company has yet to turn a profit.

image.caption: Dario Amodei has addressed concerns about the development of the AI industryImage: Don Feria/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic on Monday filed paperwork to make its stock market debut in what analysts say could be one of the biggest in history.
The initial public offering (IPO) could happen as early as November, reports say, with analysts putting the company at a valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.
What did the Anthropic founders say about the IPO?
The seven co-founders of the company, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, outlined their vision for the future of AI in a letter to potential investors.
"We believe AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history," they said.

The AI startup behind Claude also addressed the societal risks of AI as they have done before, writing that the company's leadership might have to take unusual decisions to slow down the pace of development, even if that meant falling behind competitors.
The filing toward an IPO represents a major milestone for a company that was founded just five years ago.
Money raised at the IPO could provide the company with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion.
AI is much hyped, frequently feared, and possibly overrated
What do we know about Anthropic's IPO?
Anthropic is set to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT."
But the company is yet to disclose how many shares it plans to sell and what price, leaving that space blank in its paperwork filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.
Anthropic filed confidentially with the SEC in June and that gave the agency time to go over the company's financial credentials before they were made available to the public and potential investors.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters.
Anthropic debut follows SpaceX IPO
The San Francisco-based company was founded by members who defected from OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, in 2021.
OpenAI, Anthropic's main rival, is also set to debut on the stock market next year.
Both IPOs are taking place amid growing concern about AI and the race to develop AI infrastructure, including data centers that consume vast amounts of energy.
The document filed by Anthropic shows that the company has seen massive revenue growth but is yet to turn a profit, much like its AI rivals.
Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. That compares to a loss of $13 billion in the same period a year earlier.
Despite the losses, the company said that it had $112.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30.

And as for money raised at the IPO, the offering could bring in as much as $100 billion, according to reports, surpassing the current record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX that ultimately raised $86 billion in what was the biggest IPO on record to date.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is Human Immunodeficiency Virus or HIV?
articles.summary: In recent years, the Philippines has recorded a growing number of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) cases, according to the AIDS Society of the Philippines (ASP).

blocks.text: In recent years, the Philippines has recorded a growing number of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) cases, according to the AIDS Society of the Philippines (ASP).
The ASP said HIV in the country can now be considered an epidemic due to the accelerating rate of new infections rather than just the total number of cases.
According to the ASP, the estimated total number of persons living with HIV (PLHIV) as of March 2026 is 288,000.
Meanwhile, the organization reported that by 2030, young people aged 15 to 24 are projected to comprise the majority of HIV cases if proper interventions are not implemented.
HIV is a virus that attacks the body’s immune system, specifically the CD4 cells that help fight off infections and diseases.
But how is it transmitted, and what are the available services in our country to address it?
Transmission
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), HIV is transmitted through infected body fluids such as blood, breast milk, semen, and vaginal fluids.
An untreated pregnant mother living with HIV can also pass the virus to her baby during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.
In the Philippines, the ASP reported that 13 cases of mother-to-child HIV transmission (nine male and four female) were recorded from January to March 2026.
ASP president Dr. Rossana Ditangco underscored the importance of universal HIV testing among pregnant women.

“Kaya lahat ng buntis gusto nating ipa-test kasi isa lang buntis ang ma-miss natin diyan, isang bata ‘yan na may new infection. Kaya we are pushing for universal testing of all pregnant women. Kasi ang tolerance natin for mother-to-child transmission is zero,” Ditangco said.

(That is why we want all pregnant women to be tested, because if we miss even just one pregnant mother, that is one child who will contract a new infection. That is why we are pushing for universal testing of all pregnant women—because our tolerance for mother-to-child transmission is zero.)
“... Kasi once tested, the mother can start sa treatment at hindi na niya mai-infect ang kaniyang baby,” she added.
(... Because once tested, the mother can start treatment and will no longer infect her baby.)

Common misconceptions about HIV transmission include beliefs that it spreads through handshakes, toilet seats, swimming pools, kissing, sharing utensils, sneezing, coughing, public spaces and surfaces, sweat, tears, or saliva.
Normalizing HIV Testing
In pushing for better HIV awareness in the country, advocates are aiming to normalize testing first.

The ASP said that having more people consent to HIV testing will help prevent the further rise of HIV cases nationwide—individuals diagnosed with HIV will be provided with appropriate and timely treatment, while those who test negative can be further educated on how to protect themselves.
“Kasi kung normal na ang HIV test, para ka lang nagpa-general checkup, parang nasa package lang ng primary care mo, everybody will get tested nang walang ‘keme’ ika nga,” Ditangco said.
(If HIV testing becomes normalized, it will feel like getting a standard general checkup as part of your primary care package, and everybody will get tested without hesitation.)

According to the APS, the following forms of testing are available in the country and can be accessed free of charge: Rapid Testing, Self-Testing, Community-Based Screening (CBS), and the Rapid HIV Diagnostic Algorithm (rHIVda).
Treatment and prevention
The goal of HIV treatment is to significantly lower the viral level in the body to the point where it can no longer be efficiently transmitted to others.
“Once you start treatment, bababa ‘yung virus sa katawan niya at a very significant level, hindi na siya efficient manghawa ng iba. That’s why treatment is prevention,” Ditangco explained.
(Once you start treatment, the level of the virus in your body drops significantly, making it inefficient for you to infect others. That’s why treatment is prevention.)
This principle is widely known as “U=U,” which stands for “Undetectable equals Untransmittable.”

Under Antiretroviral Therapy (ART), HIV is managed by suppressing viral replication, restoring the immune system, and significantly delaying disease progression by targeting different stages of the HIV life cycle.
According to the ASP, currently available HIV treatments have improved, meaning the virus does not easily develop drug resistance, and patients experience fewer side effects.
The group emphasized that HIV treatment in the Philippines is free under the Outpatient HIV/AIDS Treatment (OHAT) package of PhilHealth.
For prevention, individuals who are potentially exposed to HIV can take pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
PrEP comes in the form of a daily pill or a long-acting injectable taken before potential exposure to the virus. At present, oral PrEP pills are available in the Philippines.
According to Ditangco, injectable PrEP, which is administered once every six months, could soon be available in the Philippines through the Department of Health.

PEP, on the other hand, is taken by an HIV-negative person within 72 hours following a potential exposure to HIV. According to Ditangco, PEP is usually taken during unforeseen events during sexual activity—such as a condom breaking or slipping off.
PEP can also be taken after a needle-stick injury or if an individual shares needles.

Ultimately, the ASP urges a more holistic approach to addressing the HIV epidemic in the Philippines, emphasizing the need for medical assistance alongside mental health support, emotional care, and public education.

Moreover, destigmatizing HIV and supporting persons living with the virus also plays a crucial role in fostering awareness and encouraging more people to seek necessary treatment and support with acceptance rather than fear. —LDF, GMA News
